scenes.text: Your house has no windows. It's pitch black inside, even at noon.
So you cut a hole in the wall. Sunlight! Problem solved.
Until winter. Now snow is blowing straight into your living room.
So you stretch an animal skin over the hole. Warm again. But dark again.
You need something solid that light passes through. So you take sand, and heat it hotter than lava. It melts into glass.
But when you shape it into sheets, it comes out bumpy and wavy. Everything outside looks melted.
So you pour the hot glass onto a pool of melted tin. It floats on top, and spreads out perfectly flat.
Let it cool, cut it to size, and put it in the wall.
Light, warm, and you can actually see outside. Congratulations. You invented the window.
And that tin trick? It's still how most window glass in the world is made today.
